newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Townspeople take Guatemala guardsmen hostage.
newsitem.headline: Townspeople take Guatemala guardsmen hostage.

text.p: At least two agents of the Guatemala National Guard were taken hostage and another 12 were reported missing on Thursday night after a raid on the sale of contraband exploded into a violent confrontation between agents and townspeople, Guard officials said.

"We are being held hostage but thank God they are treating us well," Manuel Salvador Esquival told Reuters at 9 p.m. (0300 GMT) from the National Guard headquarters in San Marcos where he and a colleague were still being held after seven hours.

Townspeople took the building as a result of a "savage" attack in nearby San Pedro Sacatepequez by National Guard agents, said Carlos Enrique Mejia Paz, secretary of a local workers' union. He answered the telephone in Guard headquarters and directed calls to the hostages.
"We have taken the building as a way to demand that the people captured appear alive and healthy and that the merchandise is returned," he said.

There were conflicting reports of the events. Police said 100 people were occupying the National Guard building, while Mejia put the number at 600 to 1,000. He said an infant girl died as a result of injuries from tear gas bombs, but police and hospital officials could not confirm the death.
National Guard officials in the capital reported a dozen agents missing several hours after the mid-day raid.
"It's not known if they're alive," said Faustino Sanchez, a spokesman for the National Guard. But local police had no knowledge of the missing agents.
Mejia said that about a dozen townspeople were missing, including children, and merchandise was illegally confiscated in the raid.

The melee began when about 100 agents of the National Guard and riot police arrived in San Pedro, about 110 miles (180 km) from the capital, on the main market day in search of clothing from Mexico being sold illegally.

Police used tear gas when townspeople carrying machetes and sticks turned violent, Sanchez said. Members of the San Marcos Guard were nearly lynched when they tried to perform a similar operation a month ago, he said.
Witnesses from San Pedro denied that, saying police and Guardsmen opened fire and threw tear gas indiscriminately and without provocation.

"It didn't matter to them that they launched bombs into a multitude that included children, babies and elderly," said Virgilio Lopez of the San Pedro rescue squad. "Nothing like this has ever happened here. There is an infinity of losses."
Lopez said the Guard illegally captured seven people. Sanchez said two were being held and that half a truck of merchandise was confiscated.
